title: Foundry blocker (deck-tick candidate)
description: feat-foundry-blocker-requires-evidence, AC-BRE-1: a blocker without evidence is a Next Task. A deck tick's Blockers section used to be free prose, so anything could be called a blocker and the operator became the inbox. This schema gives a candidate blocker a shape a script can check BEFORE it is reported: a claim, the evidence for it, what was already tried, and a why_operator drawn from the SAME closed `escalate_when` set the contract schema already fixes (schema/acceptance-contract.schema.json, feat-foundry-contract-done-when-escalate-when AC-DWE-1) -- not redefined here in prose. `scripts/foundry_blocker_check.py` reads a list of these and partitions valid from invalid; the invalid ones are Next Tasks, not blockers.

claim.description: The one-line assertion of what is blocked and why, as it would read under the tick's Blockers section.

evidence.description: At least one concrete artifact backing the claim -- a command's captured output, a repo-relative file path, a URL, or verbatim error text. Not a restatement of the claim.

attempted.description: At least one thing the agent actually tried before escalating -- what it ran, read, or checked. A blocker with nothing attempted is a Next Task the agent has not yet worked.

why_operator.description: Member of the closed `escalate_when` set (schema/acceptance-contract.schema.json's `escalate_when` enum, feat-foundry-contract-done-when-escalate-when AC-DWE-1) -- the SAME five members, not redefined here. Anything outside this closed set is not a legitimate operator escalation.

handoff.description: OPTIONAL, deliberately UNCONSTRAINED here (no nested schema) -- the operator-handoff-schema atom (out of scope for this one, see the blocker-requires-evidence charter's Out of scope) constrains this shape next. A blocker MAY carry one today; this schema does not yet check its contents.
